For the officer joining this caseload, here is a concise orientation summary:  

**District Concentration**: Cases are concentrated in **فیصل آباد** (Faisalabad: 19 cases) and **لاہور** (Lahore: 18 cases), with **راولپنڈی** (Rawalpindi: 10 cases) as the next major hub. Smaller numbers are registered in **اسلام آباد** (Islamabad: 5), **چنیوٹ** (Chiniot: 5), **حیدر آباد** (Hyderabad: 5), **کراچی ایسٹ** (Karachi East: 5), **کراچی وسطی** (Karachi Central: 5), and **ملتان** (Multan: 1 case) [Document 1].  

**Case Mix**: Current cases (2026) include **39 Pakistan Penal Code (PPC)** cases (up from 13 in 2024), **16 Arms Ordinance 1965** cases (down from 13 in 2024), and new categories such as **CNSA 1997 (12 cases)**, **PECA 2016 (9 cases)**, **Punjab Domestic Violence Act (4 cases)**, and **Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 (2 cases)**. This reflects a shift toward addressing domestic violence, economic crimes, and broader legal issues alongside traditional offenses [Document 2].  

**Arrest Rates**: Only **11 of 73 FIRs** record at least one arrest (1 in 6.6), while **62 FIRs** have no arrests recorded [Document 3].  

**Reporting Delays**: The mean time from incident to report is **1401.3 minutes (~23.4 hours)** in 2026 (across 51 FIRs), a stark increase from **15.0 minutes** in 2024 (across 13 FIRs) [Document 4].  

**Weapon Licensing**: Of **32 weapon-register entries** reviewed, **30 recovered weapons** are recorded **without a licence**, and **2 entries** have **no licence status** confirmed [Document 5].  

This caseload requires attention to diverse legal issues, low arrest rates, delayed reporting, and high prevalence of unlicensed weapons.
